assessment.title: Grounded Growth Initial Alignment and Capability Assessment v1.1
assessment.purpose: Estimate six non-evaluative personality orientations and create provisional 0-1 evidence states for 37 developmental levers.
instructions: Answer from your behavior during the past six months, not from your ideal self.
Use ordinary behavior across contexts, not your single best or worst moment.
Choose Not applicable / insufficient experience when a role or context has not occurred.
The result is a provisional self-report estimate. It is not a diagnosis and does not prove mastery.

capability.1: Rarely demonstrated; I usually need substantial guidance
capability.2: Sometimes demonstrated with prompts, structure, or support
capability.3: Usually demonstrated in familiar, low-pressure situations
capability.5: Reliable under pressure or novelty; I can adapt or help others

core_items.prompt: When facing a new problem, I naturally want to understand its structure before acting.
I am energized by finding patterns, inconsistencies, and the most accurate explanation.
When an important decision is stalled, I would rather take responsibility for choosing a workable direction than keep gathering input.
I gain energy from initiating difficult action, even when I may be judged for the outcome.
When a group has both a task problem and a relationship problem, my attention naturally goes first to whether people feel understood and included.
Given equal free time, I am more drawn to deepening or repairing a relationship than to working alone on an idea or project.
I naturally maintain systems, commitments, and resources so they remain dependable over time.
I would rather strengthen an important responsibility or proven structure than leave it for a more novel possibility.
When a sound method already exists, I still feel pulled to test an unfamiliar alternative.
I gain energy from entering unfamiliar subjects, places, or ways of doing things even without an immediate practical payoff.
When a personally advantageous option conflicts with a principle or larger good I believe in, my attention goes first to the principle or larger good.
I am energized by questions of meaning, virtue, sacredness, beauty, or what should outlast me.
When major choices compete, I can explain which direction best fits what I believe my life is for.
I follow the same ethical standard when doing so costs me as when it benefits me.
I maintain a deliberate practice that connects me to meaning, sacredness, or reality beyond immediate self-interest.
After loss or serious setback, I can face what happened without denial and still identify a reason to continue.
I recognize my recurring defensive patterns before they fully control my behavior.
I can identify the specific emotion I am feeling, its intensity, and what triggered it.
When strongly upset, I can settle enough to choose a response I will still endorse later.
I can keep attention on the person or task I chose even when easier stimulation is available.
When I strongly want pleasure, approval, comfort, or escape, I can delay acting long enough to decide deliberately.
I begin and complete important work on schedule even when motivation is low.
When a plan fails, I revise quickly without clinging to the old approach or abandoning the goal reflexively.
I can identify the assumptions and logical steps that connect a claim to its conclusion.
When credible evidence conflicts with a belief I value, I update the belief rather than dismissing the evidence.
Before a consequential decision, I consider downstream effects, tradeoffs, feedback loops, and likely failure modes.
When learning something difficult, I use recall, practice, and feedback rather than mainly rereading or consuming explanations.
I regularly create or interpret something using both technique and personal judgment.
I maintain health routines that reliably support my energy and physical function.
I can independently maintain a clean, safe, fed, and functional household.
I use digital systems deliberately enough to protect my information and avoid being passively steered by them.
I can recognize common hazards and carry out a proportionate plan for emergencies or high-risk situations.
My financial system reliably covers obligations, foreseeable risks, and long-term goals.
When I want to create economic value, I can test a real need and adapt based on feedback.
In difficult conversations, I can state my meaning clearly and accurately summarize the other person's view before responding.
I can infer how a situation looks to someone else and then check my interpretation instead of assuming it is correct.
I state and enforce limits directly even when I risk disappointment or disapproval.
I consistently initiate, maintain, and reciprocate important relationships instead of waiting for others to carry them.
In intimate relationships, I communicate honestly about desire, consent, expectations, and vulnerability.
When someone depends on me, I provide reliable care while preserving their agency and my own limits.
After relational harm, I can own my part, seek repair, and distinguish forgiveness from restored trust.
I can identify the responsible institution and take practical civic action on an issue that matters.
I apply standards of dignity and fairness even to people or groups I dislike or disagree with.
I reliably produce useful, high-quality work and understand who depends on it.
When responsible for others, I set clear direction, invite dissent, and use authority without unnecessary control.
I regularly engage in rest, play, or celebration without turning it into optimization or numbing escape.
I deliberately seek unfamiliar or natural environments and navigate them with curiosity and proportionate preparation.
My calendar, commitments, and environment reflect my stated priorities for this season of life.
I deliberately transfer knowledge, care, opportunity, or durable work so value remains after my involvement.
I based these answers on what I have actually done during the past six months, not mainly on who I hope or believe I should be.

adaptive_capability_clarifiers.prompt: I can name the few commitments that should win when important demands conflict.
I keep promises and standards even when nobody would know if I did not.
My spiritual or contemplative beliefs influence concrete choices rather than remaining abstract ideas.
I can hold grief, uncertainty, or suffering without either minimizing it or losing all hope.
When trusted feedback contradicts my self-image, I can examine it without immediate defensiveness.
I can distinguish what I feel from what I think happened or what I want to do next.
After a destabilizing event, I can recover routines and adapt without prolonged avoidance or impulsive reaction.
I notice when my attention has drifted and can return it without needing a new burst of stimulation.
I can enjoy pleasure without repeatedly exceeding limits I chose in advance.
I maintain important routines through ordinary disruption rather than only during motivated periods.
I can remain effective when plans, roles, or expectations change unexpectedly.
I can detect when a conclusion does not actually follow from the reasons offered for it.
Before repeating a claim, I check the source, evidence quality, uncertainty, and plausible alternatives.
I can distinguish a symptom from a root cause and choose an intervention that addresses the system.
I can teach or apply what I learned after time has passed and in a different context.
I complete and share creative work rather than remaining only in inspiration, taste, or unfinished drafts.
I can adjust training, food, sleep, and medical care based on evidence from my body and qualified guidance.
I can troubleshoot ordinary household problems and recognize when professional help is required.
I can identify manipulated or low-quality digital information before acting on or sharing it.
I maintain realistic emergency knowledge, supplies, and plans appropriate to my environment.
I know my current cash flow, debt, reserves, insurance, and long-term financial plan.
I understand the incentives, costs, customers, and tradeoffs behind an economic decision or venture.
People usually leave difficult conversations knowing what I meant and feeling that I understood them.
I revise my judgment of another person when their account or new evidence contradicts my first interpretation.
I can say no, make a request, or confront disrespect without becoming passive, apologetic, or aggressive.
My close relationships receive regular time, initiative, reliability, and practical support from me.
I can discuss sexual and relational boundaries calmly before ambiguity or pressure creates a problem.
I can coordinate care, responsibilities, and limits without controlling or abandoning the person who depends on me.
When conflict recurs, I change the underlying pattern rather than only apologizing after each episode.
I participate in civic or community life through informed action rather than only opinion or outrage.
I can advocate for justice while representing opposing views fairly and resisting dehumanization.
I improve my craft through standards, deliberate practice, feedback, documentation, and reliable delivery.
People under my authority become clearer, safer, and more capable rather than merely more dependent on me.
I can rest or celebrate with full presence and return to responsibility without guilt or avoidance.
I pursue challenge and exploration without confusing recklessness, novelty, or consumption with growth.
I deliberately rebalance work, relationships, health, service, and rest as the season of life changes.
I build people, systems, traditions, or records that continue to create value without my constant presence.

adaptive_orientation_clarifiers.prompt: I would rather delay action briefly to improve my model of a problem than move immediately with an incomplete understanding.
I would rather own a difficult decision and its consequences than wait for someone else to resolve it.
I would rather invest effort in mutual understanding than win a low-stakes point or maximize a task result.
I would rather maintain an important responsibility well than chase a new opportunity that could weaken it.
I would rather explore several plausible paths than commit early to the first workable one.
I would accept meaningful personal cost for a principle or common good I deeply endorse.

lever_catalog.name: Purpose and Direction
lever_catalog.definition: Clarifies what is worth pursuing, why it matters, and how present commitments express a coherent direction.

lever_catalog.name: Values, Integrity, and Moral Courage
lever_catalog.definition: Translates ethical commitments into truthful, reliable, fair, and courageous conduct across contexts.

lever_catalog.name: Spirituality, Reverence, and Transcendence
lever_catalog.definition: Develops relationship to the sacred, ultimate concern, ritual, contemplation, vocation, and realities larger than the isolated self.

lever_catalog.name: Mortality, Suffering, Gratitude, and Hope
lever_catalog.definition: Builds the capacity to face impermanence, tragedy, loss, limitation, received life, and hope without denial.

lever_catalog.name: Self-Knowledge, Identity, and Humility
lever_catalog.definition: Improves accurate self-understanding, identity coherence, awareness of limitations and defenses, and proportionate self-regard.

lever_catalog.name: Emotional Awareness and Literacy
lever_catalog.definition: Recognizes, differentiates, names, and communicates emotions and their bodily and situational signals.

lever_catalog.name: Emotional Regulation and Resilience
lever_catalog.definition: Regulates emotion without suppression, recovers from setbacks, seeks help appropriately, and generalizes coping skills under stress.

lever_catalog.name: Attention and Presence
lever_catalog.definition: Directs attention deliberately, sustains contact with the present, and notices distraction, interpretation, and automaticity.

lever_catalog.name: Temperance and Desire Governance
lever_catalog.definition: Uses pleasure, consumption, craving, status, comfort, and impulse without being ruled by them.

lever_catalog.name: Discipline, Habits, and Follow-Through
lever_catalog.definition: Converts intentions into consistent action through habits, planning, accountability, perseverance, and completion.

lever_catalog.name: Adaptability, Uncertainty, and Learning from Failure
lever_catalog.definition: Acts under uncertainty, revises plans, tolerates change, and converts setbacks or disconfirmation into improved behavior.

lever_catalog.name: Critical Reasoning and Logic
lever_catalog.definition: Analyzes claims, arguments, assumptions, contradictions, and alternatives with disciplined reasoning.

lever_catalog.name: Evidence, Truth, and Epistemic Humility
lever_catalog.definition: Evaluates sources and evidence, tracks uncertainty, updates beliefs, and resists bias, misinformation, and overconfidence.

lever_catalog.name: Systems Thinking, Judgment, and Decision-Making
lever_catalog.definition: Understands causality, tradeoffs, risk, feedback, context, and second-order effects to make and revise sound decisions.

lever_catalog.name: Learning Agility, Memory, and Teaching
lever_catalog.definition: Acquires, organizes, practices, retains, transfers, explains, and transmits knowledge and skill.

lever_catalog.name: Creativity, Aesthetics, and Cultural Literacy
lever_catalog.definition: Creates, interprets, refines, and shares meaningful work while developing imagination, taste, cultural context, and attribution ethics.

lever_catalog.name: Physical Health, Vitality, and Embodiment
lever_catalog.definition: Maintains health, movement capacity, recovery, body literacy, bodily autonomy, and sustainable physical functioning.

lever_catalog.name: Domestic Competence and Material Self-Sufficiency
lever_catalog.definition: Operates and maintains a safe, functional home and everyday material life through practical skills and systems.

lever_catalog.name: Digital Agency, Media Literacy, and Security
lever_catalog.definition: Uses digital tools and AI competently while governing attention, verifying information, protecting identity and data, and participating responsibly online.

lever_catalog.name: Safety, Risk, and Preparedness
lever_catalog.definition: Anticipates hazards, prevents avoidable harm, responds to emergencies, and builds personal and communal resilience.

lever_catalog.name: Financial Stewardship and Provision
lever_catalog.definition: Manages cash flow, debt, saving, investing, protection, consumption, generosity, and material obligations responsibly.

lever_catalog.name: Economic Agency, Entrepreneurship, and Market Literacy
lever_catalog.definition: Understands economic systems and creates, prices, negotiates, operates, and governs value-producing activity responsibly.

lever_catalog.name: Communication and Listening
lever_catalog.definition: Listens attentively and expresses ideas, needs, feedback, stories, and arguments clearly across audiences and contexts.

lever_catalog.name: Empathy, Social Perception, and Perspective-Taking
lever_catalog.definition: Accurately perceives others' experiences, motives, emotions, needs, contexts, and viewpoints without erasing difference.

lever_catalog.name: Boundaries, Assertiveness, and Self-Respect
lever_catalog.definition: States needs and limits, protects autonomy and dignity, resists coercion, and says no or exits responsibly.

lever_catalog.name: Friendship, Belonging, and Hospitality
lever_catalog.definition: Initiates, selects, maintains, and contributes to reciprocal friendships, networks, communities, and inclusive belonging.

lever_catalog.name: Intimacy, Sexuality, and Partnership
lever_catalog.definition: Builds consensual, secure, communicative, mutually responsible intimate relationships across changing stages and forms.

lever_catalog.name: Family, Parenting, and Caregiving
lever_catalog.definition: Participates responsibly in family systems, parenting, reproduction, elder care, disability care, safeguarding, and shared household care.

lever_catalog.name: Conflict, Repair, Forgiveness, and Reconciliation
lever_catalog.definition: Navigates disagreement, de-escalates harm, apologizes, repairs trust, forgives wisely, and supports reconciliation where possible.

lever_catalog.name: Service, Citizenship, and Civic Agency
lever_catalog.definition: Contributes to community needs, understands civic channels, organizes responsibly, and builds collective capacity.

lever_catalog.name: Justice, Pluralism, and Social Responsibility
lever_catalog.definition: Understands rights, inequality, institutions, power, difference, and shared risk while preserving dignity and peaceful coexistence.

lever_catalog.name: Work, Craft, Professionalism, and Contribution
lever_catalog.definition: Builds reliable, adaptive, ethical competence and delivers useful, high-quality work with appropriate boundaries.

lever_catalog.name: Leadership, Power, Mentorship, and Institutions
lever_catalog.definition: Sets direction, uses power ethically, develops others, designs accountable institutions, and responds to conflict, crisis, corruption, and abuse.

lever_catalog.name: Play, Rest, Celebration, and Joy
lever_catalog.definition: Cultivates non-instrumental play, restoration, delight, humor, festivity, and sustainable freedom from constant optimization.

lever_catalog.name: Nature, Exploration, and Adventure
lever_catalog.definition: Builds curiosity, place-awareness, ecological relationship, travel competence, outdoor capability, wonder, and calculated challenge.

lever_catalog.name: Life Design, Balance, and Seasonality
lever_catalog.definition: Integrates competing goods, roles, capacities, seasons, transitions, reviews, ambition, contentment, and multiple legitimate pathways.

lever_catalog.name: Legacy, Generativity, and Transmission
lever_catalog.definition: Invests in people, institutions, traditions, knowledge, works, and provisions that outlast the self without confusing legacy with status.

orientation_catalog.name: Discernment
orientation_catalog.definition: Preference for understanding, truth-seeking, reflection, pattern recognition, and sound judgment.
orientation_catalog.high_expression: Pauses to understand, tests assumptions, seeks coherence, and differentiates signal from noise.
orientation_catalog.possible_excess: Analysis, detachment, hesitation, or treating lived problems as intellectual puzzles.

orientation_catalog.name: Agency
orientation_catalog.definition: Preference for initiating, asserting, deciding, persisting, and producing change.
orientation_catalog.high_expression: Moves toward difficulty, makes choices, takes responsibility, and creates momentum.
orientation_catalog.possible_excess: Control, impatience, domination, overwork, or action without sufficient listening.

orientation_catalog.name: Connection
orientation_catalog.definition: Preference for empathy, belonging, cooperation, mutual understanding, and relational attunement.
orientation_catalog.high_expression: Reads people, builds trust, includes others, and protects relationship quality.
orientation_catalog.possible_excess: Approval-seeking, enmeshment, conflict avoidance, or sacrificing truth and self-respect.

orientation_catalog.name: Stewardship
orientation_catalog.definition: Preference for responsibility, reliability, maintenance, protection, provision, and long-term continuity.
orientation_catalog.high_expression: Preserves what matters, anticipates consequences, fulfills duties, and builds durable structures.
orientation_catalog.possible_excess: Rigidity, burden, paternalism, risk aversion, or loyalty to obsolete structures.

orientation_catalog.name: Exploration
orientation_catalog.definition: Preference for novelty, experimentation, creativity, discovery, and possibility.
orientation_catalog.high_expression: Generates options, crosses boundaries, learns through experience, and adapts quickly.
orientation_catalog.possible_excess: Scattered attention, impulsivity, unfinished work, or novelty without depth.

orientation_catalog.name: Transcendence
orientation_catalog.definition: Preference for meaning, virtue, reverence, service, beauty, legacy, and realities larger than the isolated self.
orientation_catalog.high_expression: Connects action to purpose, conscience, sacred concern, or the common good.
orientation_catalog.possible_excess: Moralism, abstraction, self-sacrifice without boundaries, or bypassing practical reality.

archetypes.name: The Strategist
archetypes.core_drive: Turn clear understanding into deliberate, effective action.
archetypes.signature: Analytical, decisive, goal-directed, and comfortable making tradeoffs.
archetypes.contribution: Creates direction, chooses priorities, and converts ambiguity into an executable path.
archetypes.shadow: Can over-control, treat people as variables, or mistake decisiveness for wisdom.
archetypes.growth_edge: Practice relational awareness, receptivity, play, and respect for goods that cannot be optimized.

archetypes.name: The Counselor
archetypes.core_drive: Understand people and situations deeply enough to help them move toward clarity and repair.
archetypes.signature: Reflective, perceptive, empathic, interpretive, and skilled at seeing motives and patterns.
archetypes.contribution: Helps others name what is happening, understand competing perspectives, and make humane choices.
archetypes.shadow: Can over-analyze, absorb others' emotions, become indirect, or substitute insight for action.
archetypes.growth_edge: Strengthen boundaries, decisive action, disciplined follow-through, and tolerance for imperfect execution.

archetypes.name: The Systems Steward
archetypes.core_drive: Build coherent systems that remain reliable over time.
archetypes.signature: Structured, principled, precise, responsible, and attentive to dependencies and consequences.
archetypes.contribution: Designs durable processes, institutions, plans, and safeguards that others can trust.
archetypes.shadow: Can become rigid, perfectionistic, detached from lived experience, or loyal to systems after they stop serving people.
archetypes.growth_edge: Develop emotional fluency, adaptability, creative experimentation, and restorative play.
archetypes.display_note: Previously called The Architect; renamed to avoid confusion with the common MBTI nickname for INTJ.

archetypes.name: The Explorer
archetypes.core_drive: Discover new ideas, patterns, possibilities, and ways of seeing.
archetypes.signature: Curious, inventive, intellectually independent, open-ended, and energized by complexity.
archetypes.contribution: Expands the map, questions stale assumptions, and connects knowledge across boundaries.
archetypes.shadow: Can chase novelty, avoid commitment, intellectualize life, or leave promising work unfinished.
archetypes.growth_edge: Build follow-through, practical stewardship, embodied routines, and durable belonging.

archetypes.name: The Seeker
archetypes.core_drive: Find truth, meaning, wisdom, and a life worthy of commitment.
archetypes.signature: Contemplative, philosophically serious, self-examining, and attentive to ultimate questions.
archetypes.contribution: Provides moral and existential orientation, challenges superficial goals, and preserves depth.
archetypes.shadow: Can retreat into abstraction, spiritualize avoidable problems, or wait for certainty before living.
archetypes.growth_edge: Translate conviction into concrete action, embodiment, practical competence, and accountable relationships.

archetypes.name: The Catalyst
archetypes.core_drive: Mobilize people toward growth, action, and shared possibility.
archetypes.signature: Energetic, persuasive, socially attuned, encouraging, and comfortable initiating change.
archetypes.contribution: Creates momentum, raises confidence, and helps groups cross the gap between intention and action.
archetypes.shadow: Can rush consent, overpromise, rescue others, or confuse intensity and popularity with progress.
archetypes.growth_edge: Slow down for evidence, boundaries, systems, and patient maintenance after the initial spark.

archetypes.name: The Builder
archetypes.core_drive: Turn responsibility into concrete capability, provision, and finished results.
archetypes.signature: Practical, persistent, accountable, productive, and comfortable carrying weight.
archetypes.contribution: Makes plans real, creates stability, solves material problems, and completes difficult work.
archetypes.shadow: Can overwork, dominate, suppress emotion, or equate human worth with usefulness and output.
archetypes.growth_edge: Cultivate emotional awareness, intimacy, rest, joy, and identities not dependent on achievement.

archetypes.name: The Trailblazer
archetypes.core_drive: Open new paths through experimentation, courage, and rapid learning.
archetypes.signature: Bold, adaptable, entrepreneurial, novelty-seeking, and willing to move before certainty.
archetypes.contribution: Breaks inertia, tests possibilities, creates opportunities, and normalizes intelligent risk.
archetypes.shadow: Can become impulsive, scattered, bored by maintenance, or leave others carrying the consequences.
archetypes.growth_edge: Build discipline, risk controls, financial stewardship, reliability, and completion habits.

archetypes.name: The Reformer
archetypes.core_drive: Act on conviction to align people and institutions with a higher standard.
archetypes.signature: Purposeful, courageous, values-led, demanding, and willing to confront complacency.
archetypes.contribution: Names moral failures, organizes meaningful change, and protects ideals from becoming empty language.
archetypes.shadow: Can become self-righteous, absolutist, punitive, chronically dissatisfied, or consumed by the cause.
archetypes.growth_edge: Practice pluralism, humility, repair, proportionality, and sustainable rhythms.

archetypes.name: The Guardian
archetypes.core_drive: Protect people, relationships, and the conditions that let them thrive.
archetypes.signature: Loyal, dependable, nurturing, attentive, and sensitive to practical and relational needs.
archetypes.contribution: Creates safety, continuity, belonging, and dependable care in families and communities.
archetypes.shadow: Can overfunction, become paternalistic, avoid necessary disruption, or neglect personal needs.
archetypes.growth_edge: Strengthen boundaries, self-direction, experimentation, and the ability to let others carry responsibility.

archetypes.name: The Connector
archetypes.core_drive: Create belonging and possibility by linking people, cultures, and experiences.
archetypes.signature: Sociable, curious, expressive, inclusive, and energized by shared discovery.
archetypes.contribution: Builds networks, translates across groups, creates hospitality, and makes life feel larger.
archetypes.shadow: Can seek approval, diffuse attention, avoid depth, or mistake activity and contact for intimacy.
archetypes.growth_edge: Develop disciplined attention, evidence standards, boundaries, and sustained commitment.

archetypes.name: The Healer
archetypes.core_drive: Relieve suffering and restore dignity, trust, wholeness, and hope.
archetypes.signature: Compassionate, patient, receptive, meaning-oriented, and attentive to vulnerability.
archetypes.contribution: Supports repair, accompanies people through loss, and keeps mercy connected to human dignity.
archetypes.shadow: Can become a martyr, blur boundaries, excuse harm, or make being needed central to identity.
archetypes.growth_edge: Pair compassion with assertion, justice, accountability, and material self-stewardship.

archetypes.name: The Craftsman
archetypes.core_drive: Improve reality through disciplined skill, experimentation, and care for quality.
archetypes.signature: Hands-on, inventive, patient with iteration, standards-conscious, and absorbed by mastery.
archetypes.contribution: Produces useful and beautiful work, preserves tacit knowledge, and raises the quality of practice.
archetypes.shadow: Can become perfectionistic, narrow, isolated, or more comfortable with objects and systems than people.
archetypes.growth_edge: Connect craft to purpose, communication, belonging, teaching, and broader social consequence.

archetypes.name: The Steward
archetypes.core_drive: Preserve and transmit what is valuable across people, institutions, resources, and generations.
archetypes.signature: Faithful, patient, duty-conscious, long-term oriented, and grounded in responsibility beyond the self.
archetypes.contribution: Maintains continuity, protects shared goods, mentors successors, and prevents short-term appetite from consuming the future.
archetypes.shadow: Can become burdened, conservative by reflex, controlling, or loyal to inherited forms that need reform.
archetypes.growth_edge: Welcome creativity, experimentation, adaptability, joy, and necessary endings.

archetypes.name: The Creator
archetypes.core_drive: Express meaning and reveal possibility through imagination, beauty, and original form.
archetypes.signature: Visionary, expressive, intuitive, aesthetically sensitive, and drawn to symbolic or transformative work.
archetypes.contribution: Gives shape to what others cannot yet articulate and renews culture through art, story, design, and imagination.
archetypes.shadow: Can romanticize chaos, resist structure, confuse expression with contribution, or abandon work before refinement.
archetypes.growth_edge: Develop discipline, critical testing, material stewardship, and consistent completion.

lever_families.name: Orientation and Moral Center
lever_families.definition: The goods, commitments, virtues, sacred concerns, and responses to suffering that orient a life.

lever_families.name: Inner Governance
lever_families.definition: The capacities used to understand and regulate identity, emotion, attention, desire, behavior, and adaptation.

lever_families.name: Thought, Learning, and Imagination
lever_families.definition: The capacities used to reason, establish truth, make judgments, learn, teach, create, and interpret culture.

lever_families.name: Embodied and Practical Agency
lever_families.definition: The capacities needed to inhabit a body, maintain a life, use technology, manage risk, and steward material resources.

lever_families.name: Relationship and Care
lever_families.definition: The capacities needed to communicate, understand others, preserve boundaries, belong, love, care, and repair.

lever_families.name: Contribution, Society, and Power
lever_families.definition: The capacities used to contribute through service, justice, work, leadership, and responsible participation in institutions.

lever_families.name: Integration and Flourishing
lever_families.definition: The capacities used to rest, explore, balance life across seasons, and transmit value beyond the self.

revision_notes: Fixed per-question timing so selecting an answer no longer resets the clock.
Reduced the severity of timing and response-style penalties.
Reworded orientation items to distinguish connection, stewardship, agency, exploration, and transcendence more clearly.
Renamed The Architect archetype to The Systems Steward to avoid collision with the MBTI INTJ nickname.
Results now display raw self-report, calibrated estimate, and confidence separately.
Added clearer archetype confidence and interpretation language.
